business_problem: Muscogee Nation Gaming Enterprises needed to improve visibility across a complex gaming and hospitality network, discover unknown assets, and prioritize vulnerability remediation between periodic scans.
solution_summary: Muscogee Nation Gaming Enterprises deployed Armis from ServiceNow as an always-on asset-intelligence platform across its physical and virtual estate, including VMware vSphere. Armis passively identifies connected assets, monitors communications and anomalous traffic, and aggregates findings from security tools. AI-powered classification and risk prioritization help the team decide which vulnerabilities to address and automatically route tickets to the right owners. Armis data and risk assessments are integrated into Splunk for security investigations, while a network-mapper integration provides switch-port tracking. Dashboards expose asset details to teams with granular access controls. The deployment found more than 10,000 assets missed by the previous tool and detects vulnerabilities two weeks faster, helping the security team reduce exposure while maintaining operations across 12 locations.

solution_components.name: Armis from ServiceNow
solution_components.role: Continuously discovers assets, analyzes traffic, and prioritizes security risks with AI-powered asset intelligence.

solution_components.name: VMware vSphere
solution_components.role: Provides the virtualized server environment whose assets Armis discovers and monitors.

solution_components.name: Splunk
solution_components.role: Receives Armis device data, risk assessments, and alerts for security investigations.

solution_components.name: Network mapper
solution_components.role: Provides real-time switch-port tracking to locate and secure connected assets.

data_flow: Armis continuously ingests device communications and security findings across physical and vSphere assets, applies AI-powered classification and prioritization, sends alerts to Splunk, and routes tickets to responsible teams; network-mapper data supports switch-port location.
business_outcome: Armis found more than 10,000 previously unknown assets, detects vulnerabilities two weeks faster, saves over 10 hours per month in vulnerability scoping, and saves up to four hours per month by automating ticket ownership.
